preprocess_precision_rationale: the same checkpoint and the same physical resampling as @1.0.0
@1.0.0 rounds to uint8 in interpolate_depth and again in resize_stack, so the 1.18x upscale from 9.362 um toward 7.91 um is forced back onto 256 levels twice

the model input is float32: infer_map applies clamp(0,200)/200, so no uint8 stage is required anywhere in the chain. The divisor is the clip value itself, not 255: upstream's contract is clip(0, CFG.max_clip_value) followed by A.ToFloat(max_value=CFG.max_clip_value). This said /255 until an external audit read it against the runner; dividing by 255 compresses the input to 78.4% of the contrast range the model was trained on, and a reimplementation built from this profile would have inherited that
@1.1.0 keeps interpolate_depth and resize_stack in float32 and quantizes zero times
numerically different output; @1.0.0 stays frozen and reproducible and remains the routed lane until a control compares the two

comparability: a probability map from this profile may not be pooled with a @1.0.0 map in one stability ensemble
the boundary valid mask widens slightly because bilinear values below 0.5 no longer round to 0
